subject: PHI minimization, retention windows, and destructive options — Q&A
messages:
From: Dr. Emily Choi <emily.choi@medsecure.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medsecure.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Questions: retention windows + destructive redaction options for PHI

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week — impressed with the latency numbers. Our security team has two outstanding items before we proceed to pilots:

1) We need clear options for retention windows for PHI-derived artifacts (both embeddings and metadata) and the operational guarantees for destructive deletion (how irreversible is the deletion, audit trail).
2) We want to understand the tradeoffs between "destructive redaction at ingest" vs "pseudonymize & reversible key store" for use cases where we may need to re-link records for care continuity.

Can you outline practical options, timelines to implement each on Redwood Private (VPC) and what evidence / logs you can provide to satisfy auditors? If you have a one-page comparison matrix, that would be ideal.

Appreciate a short summary so we can pass to legal and privacy.

- Emily
Dr. Emily Choi
Head of Privacy & Compliance, MedSecure Health

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Emily Choi <emily.choi@medsecure.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions: retention windows + destructive redaction options for PHI

Emily — thanks for the clear ask. Below is a concise matrix of practical approaches we’ve implemented with other regulated customers, plus the artifact/evidence each option yields. Attached is a short PDF with implementation notes.

High-level options (summary):

A) Short retention + immutable deletion (recommended for high-risk PHI):
  - What: Retain full text & derived artifacts for N days (suggest 30–90d), then irreversibly delete token streams, embeddings, and metadata.
  - How: Overwrite and crypto-shred object keys (KMS/HSM key rotation + key destruction), remove KV cache, and run a background job to zero out storage blocks where possible on customer-managed disk.
  - Evidence: Deletion audit record (UID, timestamp, operator), KMS key-shred logs, S3 object lifecycle transitions, and a signed digest that indicates retention job completion.
  - Tradeoffs: Recovery impossible after deletion, impacts long-term analytics and model fine-tuning.

B) Pseudonymization with reversible key store (useful for care continuity):
  - What: At ingest, replace direct identifiers with deterministic tokens; raw identifiers are encrypted with customer-controlled HSM keys stored in the Private deployment.
  - How: Tokenization service with deterministic salt per-tenant; encrypted identifier store accessible under strict ACL + MFA/approval workflow.
  - Evidence: Access logs to key material (HSM audit), tokenization logs, KMS/HSM access manifests, and retention labels indicating re-link windows.
  - Tradeoffs: Enables re-linking but adds key management overhead and increases attack surface if keys are not managed under HSM.

C) Two-tier approach (recommended for mixed workflows):
  - What: Keep pseudonymized linkability for a short window (e.g., 90d) and automatically crypto-shred keys and destructively delete identifiers after that window, while retaining non-identifying analytics artifacts longer.
  - How: Policy engine controls TTLs for key shards and data tiers; automated eDiscovery hold can pause the shredding process per-record.
  - Evidence: Combined logs: TTL events, key-shred confirmation, and analytics retention manifests.
  - Tradeoffs: More operational complexity but gives balance between safety and clinical needs.

Operational notes and timelines:
  - Private deployment (VPC): Options A–C are supported. Estimated delivery for configuration and runbooks:
    * Option A: 2 weeks configuration + 1 week verification and audit artifacts.
    * Option B: 3–4 weeks to wire HSM integrations and deterministic tokenization with audit hooks.
    * Option C: 4–6 weeks to implement policy engine TTLs and eDiscovery hold paths.

Artifacts we provide for audits: signed deletion manifests, KMS key rotation & shred logs (HSM-supplied), per-record deletion events (UID + timestamp), retention policy configuration snapshots, and sample scripts to reproduce verification runs on your side.

Next steps: If you’d like, Marissa can draft contract language for retention windows and Naomi can outline the audit evidence we will ship with the pilot. Happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk through the PDF.

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Questions: retention windows + destructive redaction options for PHI

Karthik / Naomi — forwarding Emily’s original note and Karthik’s summary. Few contract/ops points we should propose back: 

- Retention SLA language: define "PHI short window" (we suggest 60 days) and list irreversible deletion as a customer-triggered lifecycle event; include confirmation digest delivered within 24 hours of completion.
- eDiscovery hold: require per-record hold API that marks a UID and prevents automated shredding; provide an admin audit view.
- Evidence package: (1) signed deletion manifest, (2) HSM key destruction receipt, (3) runbook for verification.
- Temp access for re-linking: if they choose Option B, require 2-person approval + timeboxed access windows logged to HSM.

Naomi — can you draft the legal phrasing for the retention clause and the sample evidence list? I’ll prepare the pricing impact (small uplift for HSM ops).

On another note, Emily asked for a one-page matrix — I used the attached PDF as the basis but we should make a redlined version for legal.

— Marissa
VP, Solutions & GTM Ops

Karthik / Marissa / Naomi — thanks for the clear write-up and the PDF. After an internal review, MedSecure is comfortable proceeding with Option C (two-tier) for the pilot, with the following ask: 

1) Initial configuration: 90-day reversible pseudonymization window, after which keys are crypto-shredded unless a per-record eDiscovery hold is active.
2) Deletion evidence: we require a signed CSV manifest per deletion job (UID, deletion_ts, operator_id) and HSM key destruction receipts; we also require a retention-policy snapshot for each tenant version.
3) Timeline: target pilot start 2026-12-01. Can Redwood deliver config and evidence runbook by 2026-11-19?

Please confirm and outline any blockers (esp. any lead time required for HSM provisioning in our VPC). Also please share the sample_deletion_audit.csv you referenced.

Best,
Emily
